beats.text: You'll probably yawn before this video ends.
In one study, over a quarter of people yawned just from reading about yawning.
Watching someone yawn works even better. Most people caught it within five minutes.
But why do we yawn at all? Science still doesn't know.
One idea: it cools your brain. Another: it's about empathy, since people who catch yawns easily may be more tuned in to others. Neither is settled.
So if you yawned just now? Nobody knows exactly why. Comment if you did.

sources: Provine (1986). Yawning as a stereotyped action pattern and releasing stimulus. Ethology 72. Most subjects yawned within 5 min of viewing videotaped yawns; over 1/4 yawned while reading about yawning (about 3/4 yawned or thought about it); thinking about yawning effective in the majority. Via baillement.com (Provine excerpt).
Function unresolved; brain-cooling hypothesis (Gallup) and empathy link debated. Via ZME Science overview.
